A year-on-year reading of 0.0% or below would require a sharp contraction, and it can't be ruled out given tariff headwinds. The market price of 2.5% is reasonable. I put it slightly higher at about 4% to allow for the calendar-adjustment ambiguity.

rows.question: Will Germany GDP growth in Q2 2026 be between 0.1% and 0.3%?
rows.rationale: The market resolves on Destatis's year-on-year, price-adjusted growth rate for Q2 2026. Destatis's flash release reports both price- and calendar-adjusted and price-adjusted-only year-on-year figures, so which one counts is somewhat ambiguous. My view of the German economy as of mid-2026 is uncertain: quarter-on-quarter growth was weak, roughly 0.1–0.3%, and fiscal stimulus should be lifting year-on-year growth toward about 0.5–1%. The 2025 quarters were roughly flat after the Q1 2025 rise, so a Q2 2026 year-on-year figure in the 0.2–0.8 range seems likely. Calendar effects could swing the unadjusted figure. A narrow 0.1–0.3 bracket probably carries about 20–30% probability, so I stay close to the market price of 0.22.
